admission.justification: Realized where the closures were made — the watcher action maps, the cgc process control and the lifecycle service — and the mistake it prevents is deleting a symbol a surviving stop path still reaches, which would break the safety and cleanup guarantees this same leaf must keep.

applicability: Every retired provider module, symbol, asset and setting key of this repository.
conditions: A caller inventory exists for the exact candidate that removes the subject.
A surviving production root is traced before a closure is declared.
exclusions: Deleting a module because its first scan says remove, while a retained stop or safety root still calls it.
A facade export, an import, or a generic action argument standing in for a production root.

evidence: mcp/tests/test_l192_provider_status_closure.py (6 cases: allowlist, both action maps, ValueError for start/status, retired helpers, image retained) and 260928-MIK-L192-repair-audit-provenance-handoff-v2.md (removal delta map). The module is one of the two repaired under the scoped pyright finding — two `cast(McpRuntimeConfig, …)` wrappers only — so its assertions are the ones that ran before and after that repair unchanged.

statement: Code was removed by caller and not by module: every provider symbol, asset and key carries a recorded caller disposition, and the two closures finished only after their surviving production roots were shown to reach no start or status path (the watcher status/start branches, then the 15-function cgc start chain).
